examples.en: The letter you wrote to your grandmother is very warm.
A letter usually starts with a greeting.
I learned how to write a letter in class.

examples.ko: 이 편지글에는 친구에 대한 마음이 잘 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: This letter is full of feeling for the friend.
A letter-writing question came up on the test.

examples.ko: 오래된 편지글을 읽으니까 옛날 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Reading an old letter reminds me of the past.

explain: '편지'는 보내는 물건 자체를 말할 때도 많지만, '편지글'은 글의 형식이나 내용을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 쓰기 수업이나 시험에서 '편지글 쓰기'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '편지' often refers to the letter as an item you send, while '편지글' is used when talking about the form or content of the writing. That is why it often appears in writing classes and tests, as in '편지글 쓰기'.

examples.en: On the news, announcers always use standard Korean.

examples.ko: 저는 부산 사람이라 표준말이 조금 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm from Busan, so standard Korean feels a little awkward to me.
How are dialects and standard Korean different?
Let's check in the dictionary whether this word is standard.
I practice giving presentations in standard Korean every day.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구는 사투리보다 표준말이 더 알아듣기 쉽대요.
examples.en: My foreign friend says standard Korean is easier to understand than dialects.

explain: 사투리의 반대말로 많이 써요. 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '표준어'라고 하고, 일상 대화에서는 '표준말'이라고 편하게 말해요.
explain_en: It is often used as the opposite of '사투리' (dialect). In writing or formal settings people say '표준어', while '표준말' is the more casual way to say it in everyday talk.

examples.en: Korean has many ways of expressing politeness.

examples.ko: 같은 뜻도 표현법에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
examples.en: Even the same meaning feels different depending on how it is expressed.
I learned ways to express feelings from this book.
Ways of greeting differ a little from country to country.

examples.ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 공손한 표현법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me a polite way to ask for a favor.
Please explain it again in simpler words.

explain: '표현'이 말이나 글로 나타낸 것 자체라면, '표현법'은 그것을 나타내는 방식을 말해요. '감정 표현법', '인사 표현법'처럼 앞에 주제를 붙여서 자주 써요.
explain_en: While '표현' is the thing expressed itself, '표현법' is the way of expressing it. It is often used with a topic in front, like '감정 표현법' (ways to express feelings) or '인사 표현법' (ways to greet).

en: blue or green hue; bluish tint

examples.en: The sea sparkles blue in the early morning.
That bottle gives off a soft bluish glow.
A bluish tint began to appear in the dawn sky.

examples.ko: 푸른빛 원피스가 너한테 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The blue dress really suits you.
At the forest lake, all you can see is blue-green.
Just looking at blue makes my mind feel refreshed.

explain: '푸르다'는 하늘이나 바다 같은 파란색뿐 아니라 풀과 나무의 초록색에도 써요. 그래서 '푸른빛'도 파란 느낌인지 초록 느낌인지는 대상을 보고 알 수 있어요. '푸른빛이 돌다', '푸른빛을 띠다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '푸르다' covers not only the blue of sky and sea but also the green of grass and trees. So '푸른빛' may feel blue or green depending on what it describes. It often appears as '푸른빛이 돌다' or '푸른빛을 띠다'.

examples.en: Small wildflowers have bloomed along the road.
The children picked wildflowers and made flower rings.
I felt spring in a tiny wildflower.
The walking path is full of wildflowers.

examples.ko: 풀꽃 이름을 하나도 몰라서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know any of the wildflower names, so I took photos.

examples.ko: 풀꽃은 작지만 자세히 보면 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: Wildflowers are small, but they are really pretty up close.

explain: 꽃집에서 파는 꽃이나 화단의 꽃과 달리, 들이나 길가에서 저절로 자라는 작은 꽃을 말할 때 써요. '들꽃'과 비슷하게 쓰지만 '풀꽃'은 풀처럼 작고 소박한 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike florist flowers or garden flowers, it refers to small flowers that grow by themselves in fields or by the road. It is close to '들꽃', but '풀꽃' sounds smaller and more modest, like the grass itself.

examples.en: I dip green peppers in soybean paste and eat them.
This green pepper is much hotter than I thought.
I bought a bag of green peppers at the market.
I stir-fried green peppers together with anchovies.
Green peppers are green because they are not ripe yet.

examples.ko: 쌈장이랑 풋고추만 있어도 밥 한 그릇이 뚝딱이에요.
examples.en: With just ssamjang and green peppers, I can finish a bowl of rice in no time.

explain: '풋-'은 덜 익었다는 뜻이라서 빨갛게 익은 고추와 구별할 때 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '고추'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: The prefix '풋-' means not fully ripe, so the word is used to tell these apart from red, ripened peppers. In daily life people also often just say '고추'.

examples.en: I made French toast on Saturday morning.
This café's French toast is delicious.
I poured plenty of syrup on the French toast.

examples.ko: 달걀이랑 우유만 있으면 프렌치토스트 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: With just eggs and milk, you can make French toast.
One French toast and a coffee for brunch, please.
French toast is fine even when made with stale bread.

explain: 그냥 '토스트'는 빵을 굽거나 달걀, 채소를 넣은 간식을 말하는 경우가 많고, '프렌치토스트'는 달걀물에 적셔서 구운 빵이에요. 카페 메뉴에서 자주 보고, 보통 시럽이나 과일과 함께 먹어요.
explain_en: Plain '토스트' often means grilled bread or a snack with egg and vegetables, while '프렌치토스트' is bread soaked in egg mixture and pan-fried. You often see it on café menus, usually served with syrup or fruit.

examples.en: These days I feel very tired all day.

examples.ko: 오래 운전한 날은 피로감을 많이 느껴요.
examples.en: On days I drive for a long time, I feel very fatigued.
After taking medicine, the fatigue eased a little.

examples.ko: 피로감 때문에 회의 내내 집중하기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Because of the fatigue, it was hard to concentrate during the whole meeting.
With body aches and fatigue on top, I took a day off.
I'm suffering from fatigue and feel sleepy even during the day.

explain: '피로'는 몸이 지친 상태 자체이고, '피로감'은 그렇게 느끼는 기분이에요. 그래서 '피로감을 느끼다', '피로감이 쌓이다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '피곤하다'를 훨씬 편하게 써요.
explain_en: '피로' is the state of being worn out, and '피로감' is the feeling of it, so we say '피로감을 느끼다' or '피로감이 쌓이다'. In everyday speech, '피곤하다' is the more casual choice.

examples.ko: 장마철에 비가 계속 오면 피부병이 늘어요.
examples.en: When it keeps raining in the monsoon season, skin diseases increase.
The puppy caught a skin disease, so we went to the vet.

examples.ko: 피부병은 손으로 긁으면 더 심해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: A skin disease can get worse if you scratch it.

examples.ko: 피부병 약을 하루에 두 번 발라요.
examples.en: I apply the skin medicine twice a day.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 피부병 치료는 꾸준히 해야 한다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said skin disease treatment must be kept up steadily.

examples.ko: 홍수 뒤에는 피부병과 감기가 돌기 쉬워요.
examples.en: After a flood, skin diseases and colds easily spread.

explain: '피부병에 걸리다'처럼 '걸리다'와 함께 써요. 가벼운 문제는 '피부 트러블'이라고 많이 말하고, '피부병'은 병원에서 치료가 필요한 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '걸리다', as in '피부병에 걸리다'. For minor problems people often say '피부 트러블', while '피부병' sounds more like something that needs medical treatment.

examples.en: On the way home from school, I ate tteokbokki with a friend.
It rained, so the way home from school was a mess.
Children's way home from school must be safe.
I bought ice cream at the convenience store on my way home from school.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 하굣길마다 같은 골목을 지났어요.
examples.en: As a child, I passed the same alley every day on the way home.
Cherry blossoms are in full bloom along the way home from school.

explain: 학교에 갈 때는 '등굣길', 집에 돌아올 때는 '하굣길'이라고 해서 짝으로 외우면 좋아요. '-길'은 '그때 가는 길'이라는 느낌이라 '퇴근길', '출근길'과 같은 방식으로 써요.
explain_en: The pair is '등굣길' (way to school) and '하굣길' (way home from school), so learn them together. The ending '-길' gives a sense of the route you take at that time, just like '출근길' and '퇴근길'.

examples.en: The younger students greeted their seniors in the hallway.

examples.ko: 저는 하급생을 도와주는 동아리 활동을 해요.
examples.en: I do a club activity that helps younger students.
I told the younger student the answer to the problem they didn't know.
When I was an underclassman, the seniors were scary.
My senior passed down a school uniform to a younger student.
Younger and older students clean the playground together.

explain: 반대말은 '상급생'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 학년이 낮은 사람을 보통 '후배'라고 부르고, '하급생'은 학교 안내문이나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The opposite is '상급생' (upperclassman). In everyday talk people usually call a lower-grade student a '후배', while '하급생' is seen more in school notices and writing.

examples.en: My grandfather passed away last year.

examples.ko: 아이는 하늘나라에 있는 엄마에게 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: The child wrote a letter to her mother in heaven.
In the fairy tale, an angel who lives in heaven appears.
Grandfather, I hope you are happy in heaven too.

examples.ko: 저 구름 위에 하늘나라가 있을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think there's a heavenly land above those clouds.
I watched a cartoon about the world in the sky.

explain: 종교에서 말하는 천국이나 동화 속 하늘 위의 세계를 부드럽게 말할 때 써요. 특히 돌아가신 분을 이야기할 때 '하늘나라에 계시다'처럼 쓰면 더 따뜻하게 들려요.

phrases.en: My grandmother passed away last winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '죽다' 대신 쓰는 부드럽고 조심스러운 표현이에요. 가족이나 가까운 사람의 죽음을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft, gentle way to say someone died, used instead of '죽다'. Often used for family or close people.

explain_en: It softly refers to heaven in religion or a world in the sky in fairy tales. When speaking of someone who has passed away, saying '하늘나라에 계시다' sounds gentler and warmer.

examples.en: As evening came, the lake was tinted sky-blue.
My friend came out wearing a sky-blue dress.
That child's eyes are a clear sky-blue.
We went on a picnic on a day when the sky was a lovely color.
Just looking at sky-blue feels refreshing.
I was given a ceramic piece that looks like the color of the sky.

explain: '하늘색'과 거의 같은 색을 말하지만, '하늘빛'은 색 이름보다 하늘에서 느껴지는 빛깔이라는 느낌이 있어서 글이나 시에서 더 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '하늘색'이 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It refers to almost the same color as '하늘색', but '하늘빛' feels more like the hue you sense from the sky than a plain color name, so it appears more in writing and poems. In speech, '하늘색' is more common.

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the sewer got blocked.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 하수도 공사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood is having sewer work done.
A smell was coming up from the sewer, so I reported it.

examples.ko: 시청에서 낡은 하수도를 새로 바꾸기로 했어요.
examples.en: The city hall decided to replace the old sewer.
Water that flows into the sewer goes to a treatment plant.

examples.ko: 하수도는 우리 눈에 잘 안 보이지만 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: Sewers are hard to see, but they are absolutely necessary.

explain: 쓰고 난 더러운 물이 흘러가는 길이에요. 깨끗한 물이 들어오는 '상수도'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is the system that carries away used, dirty water. It is easy to remember as a pair with '상수도', which brings in clean water.

examples.en: I was a boarder during university.

examples.ko: 하숙집 아주머니는 하숙생들에게 밥을 해 주세요.
examples.en: The landlady cooks meals for the boarders.
I heard one more boarder is moving in.
I became friends with the boarder in the next room.
A boarder has to pay for the room every month.

examples.ko: 우리 집에도 하숙생을 받아 볼까 해요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of taking in a boarder at our house too.

explain: 하숙은 남의 집에서 방을 빌리고 보통 식사도 함께 받는 거예요. 혼자 방을 구해서 직접 해 먹으며 사는 '자취생'과 구별해서 말해요.
explain_en: '하숙' means renting a room in someone's house, usually with meals included. It is different from a '자취생', who rents a place alone and cooks for themselves.

examples.en: I went to the store to buy my son's school uniform.
The uniform got too small, so I had a new one made.
School uniforms these days are comfortable and pretty.
The school uniform shop sells uniform sets.

examples.ko: 졸업식 날 학생복 차림으로 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On graduation day, I took photos in my school uniform.
Please attach a name tag to the school uniform.

explain: 학교 학생이 입는 옷을 말하지만, 일상에서는 보통 '교복'이라고 더 자연스럽게 말해요. '학생복'은 '학생복 매장'처럼 옷을 파는 곳이나 상품을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to clothes worn by students, but in daily life '교복' sounds more natural. '학생복' often appears when talking about shops or products, as in '학생복 매장'.

examples.ko: 성인 학습자의 특성을 생각해서 수업을 준비해요.
examples.en: I prepare the class thinking about the characteristics of adult learners.

examples.ko: 이 사전은 초급 학습자를 위해 만들었어요.
examples.en: This dictionary was made for beginner learners.
Each learner studies at a different speed.

examples.ko: 한국어 학습자가 많이 하는 실수를 알아봐요.
examples.en: Let's look at mistakes that learners of Korean often make.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 학습자에게 매일 문제를 보내 줘요.
examples.en: This app sends problems to learners every day.

examples.ko: 학습자는 모르는 내용을 바로 질문할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Learners can ask right away about what they don't understand.

explain: '학생'은 학교에 다니는 사람을 떠올리게 하지만, '학습자'는 학교 밖에서 배우는 사람까지 모두 포함해요. 교재, 앱, 연구 글처럼 배우는 사람을 설명하는 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '학생' makes you think of someone attending school, but '학습자' includes anyone who is learning, even outside school. You often see it in textbooks, apps and research writing that describe people who study.

examples.ko: 아이가 한군데 가만히 앉아 있지를 못해요.
examples.en: The child can't sit still in one place.
Please gather the luggage in one place.
I'll stop by just one more place and then go home.
This piece of clothing is torn in one spot.

examples.ko: 한군데서 오래 일하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to work in one place for a long time.
This weekend I have no plans anywhere.

explain: '한 곳'과 뜻은 비슷하지만 '한군데'는 말할 때 더 편하게 붙여서 써요. '한군데도 없다'처럼 뒤에 '없다'가 오면 '한 곳도 없다'는 강한 부정이 돼요.
explain_en: It means about the same as '한 곳', but '한군데' is written as one word and feels more casual in speech. With '없다' after it, as in '한군데도 없다', it gives a strong negative: not even one place.

examples.en: We have lived in the same neighborhood since we were little.
He is a friend from my neighborhood, so we meet often.
We live in the same neighborhood, but I don't even know their name.
We aren't in the same neighborhood, but we live close.
We lived in the same neighborhood, so we went to school together.
The neighborhood people gathered and held a feast.

explain: '같은 동네'와 거의 같은 뜻인데, '한동네'는 가깝고 정이 있는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '한동네 친구', '한동네에 살다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '같은 동네', but '한동네' carries a feeling of closeness and warmth. It is usually used in phrases like '한동네 친구' or '한동네에 살다'.

examples.en: The Korean people eat tteokguk on Lunar New Year.
Koreans living abroad also learn Hangeul.
I'm studying the history of the Korean people.
If you're Korean, everyone knows this song.
I tried a traditional Korean game.
The Korean people have eaten rice for a long time.

explain: '한국 사람'은 지금 한국에 사는 사람을 떠올리기 쉽지만, '한민족'은 같은 민족이라는 점을 강조해서 해외에 사는 사람까지 함께 말할 때 써요. 뉴스, 역사, 행사 이름에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '한국 사람' tends to suggest people living in Korea now, but '한민족' stresses a shared ethnic identity and can include Koreans living overseas too. It often appears in news, history and event titles.

examples.en: I had lunch with my parents at a hanjeongsik restaurant.
In a hanjeongsik meal, a great many side dishes come out.
When guests come, we treat them to hanjeongsik.
Please make a reservation for the hanjeongsik course.
We chose a quiet hanjeongsik restaurant for the families' first meeting.
I wanted to eat hanjeongsik, so I went to Insa-dong.

explain: 밥, 국, 찌개와 여러 반찬을 한 상에 차려 주는 한국 전통식 코스예요. 간단한 '백반'보다 격식 있고 가격도 높은 편이라, 부모님 모시기나 상견례처럼 특별한 자리에서 자주 가요.
explain_en: It is a traditional Korean course with rice, soup, stew and many side dishes set out on one table. It is more formal and usually pricier than a simple '백반', so people often go for special occasions like taking parents out or a family-introduction meeting.

examples.en: I was so happy when I received the certificate of acceptance.
Please keep your certificate safe.
Yesterday my certificate arrived by mail.

examples.ko: 등록할 때 합격증 사본을 내야 해요.
examples.en: I have to submit a copy of the acceptance certificate when I register.
My name is written on the certificate.

examples.ko: 합격증으로 등록 절차를 밟을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can go through the registration procedure with the certificate.

explain: 시험이나 입학, 자격 심사에 붙었다는 것을 보여 주는 종이나 증명서예요. 합격했다는 소식을 알리는 글은 '합격 통지서'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a paper or document proving you passed an exam, admission or qualification review. A notice informing you of the result is also called a '합격 통지서'.

examples.en: In summer I often wear hot pants at home.

examples.ko: 그 핫팬츠가 너무 짧은 것 같아요.
examples.en: Those hot pants seem too short.
I wore a long T-shirt with the hot pants.
Hot pants are too cold to wear in winter, right?

examples.ko: 동생이 핫팬츠 한 벌을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bought a pair of hot pants.
I cut my jeans and made them into hot pants.

explain: 매우 짧은 반바지를 말해요. 길이가 보통인 바지는 '반바지'라고 하고, 몸에 붙고 아주 짧은 것을 '핫팬츠'라고 구별해 써요. 옷을 셀 때는 '한 벌'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means extremely short shorts. Ordinary shorts are called '반바지', and '핫팬츠' is used for the very short, fitted kind. Use '한 벌' to count them.

examples.en: I saw an old sundial in person at the museum.
A sundial tells the time using a shadow.

examples.ko: 흐린 날에는 해시계가 시간을 못 알려 줘요.
examples.en: On cloudy days, a sundial can't tell the time.

examples.ko: 해시계로 낮 시간을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell the daytime hours with a sundial.
I stood a stick on the sundial and watched the shadow.
I made a model sundial myself.

explain: 해의 그림자로 시간을 재는 옛날 시계예요. 물이 흐르는 걸로 재는 '물시계'와 함께 역사 수업에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is an old clock that measures time by the shadow of the sun. It often comes up in history classes together with the '물시계', which uses flowing water.

examples.en: I'm happy because I bought a used book cheaply.
Even a used book can be given as a gift if it is clean.
I sell books I've finished reading to a secondhand bookstore.
I like the smell of old books, so I go often.

examples.ko: 이 헌책에는 누가 쓴 메모가 있어요.
examples.en: This used book has notes someone wrote in it.
I studied with a used book instead of a new one.

explain: '헌-'은 낡고 오래된 것 앞에 붙어서 '헌 옷', '헌책'처럼 써요. 반대말은 '새 책'이고, 말할 때는 '중고책'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: The prefix '헌-' attaches to worn, old things, as in '헌 옷' and '헌책'. The opposite is '새 책', and people also say '중고책' in speech.

examples.en: Yesterday I bought books cheaply at a used bookstore.
There is one old used bookstore in my neighborhood.
Every weekend I go browsing at a used bookstore with a friend.
The used bookstore owner recommended a book to me.

examples.ko: 헌책방은 책이 쌓여 있어서 길 찾기가 어려워요.
examples.en: In a used bookstore, books are piled up, so it's hard to find your way.

examples.ko: 졸업한 뒤에도 그 헌책방을 가끔 찾아가요.
examples.en: Even after graduating, I sometimes visit that used bookstore.

explain: 새 책을 파는 '서점'과 달리 이미 읽은 책을 사고파는 가게예요. 가격이 싸고 오래된 책을 만날 수 있어서 구경하러 가는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: Unlike a '서점' that sells new books, this shop buys and sells books that have already been read. Prices are low and you can find old books, so many people go just to browse.

examples.en: They're twins, so I get confused about who is who.
The roads were complicated, so I lost my sense of direction.
Similar words keep confusing me, which is hard.

examples.ko: 날짜가 헛갈리지 않게 달력에 적어 두세요.
examples.en: Write it on the calendar so you don't mix up the dates.

examples.ko: 두 사람 이름이 헛갈릴 때가 있어요.
examples.en: There are times I mix up the two people's names.

examples.ko: 설명이 너무 어려워서 더 헛갈리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The explanation is so hard that I think it's confusing me even more.

explain: '헷갈리다'로도 쓰고 둘 다 맞는 말이에요. 두 가지가 비슷해서 구별이 안 되거나 정신이 혼란스러울 때 써요. '헷갈려요'가 입에 더 익숙하다고 느끼는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: It can also be written '헷갈리다', and both forms are correct. Use it when two things are similar and hard to tell apart, or when your mind is muddled. Many people find '헷갈려요' more familiar to say.

en: being in vain; coming to nothing

examples.en: I prepared hard, but it all came to nothing.
Apologizing now is pointless.
I feel like I did nothing but useless work all day.
Everything ended up being in vain.
All that effort wasn't for nothing.
Nobody should think it's a waste.

explain: 애쓴 일이 아무 결과도 없을 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '헛수고'가 있는데, 둘 다 '헛-'이 붙어서 '소용없다'는 느낌이 있어요. '헛일이 되다', '헛일이다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when effort leads to no result. A similar word is '헛수고', and both carry the prefix '헛-', which gives a sense of uselessness. It is commonly said as '헛일이 되다' or '헛일이다'.

examples.en: I tied my injured leg tightly with a piece of cloth.
I made doll clothes from scraps of cloth.
Please wet a cloth and wipe it.

examples.ko: 낡은 헝겊이라도 버리지 말고 모아 두세요.
examples.en: Even old scraps of cloth, don't throw them away, keep them.

examples.ko: 헝겊을 덧대서 구멍 난 바지를 고쳤어요.
examples.en: I patched the pants with a piece of cloth to fix the hole.
A piece of cloth fades in color when used for a long time.

explain: '천'은 옷감 전체를 넓게 부르는 말이고, '헝겊'은 작은 천 조각이나 낡은 천을 말할 때 더 잘 어울려요. 그래서 '헝겊 인형', '헝겊 조각'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '천' is the broad word for fabric, while '헝겊' suits small scraps or worn cloth better. That is why it appears in phrases like '헝겊 인형' (rag doll) and '헝겊 조각' (scrap of cloth).

examples.en: I washed my hair and dried it with a hair dryer.
The hair dryer broke, so I bought a new one.
Don't hold the hair dryer too close.
The hair dryer is in the drawer.
The air from this hair dryer is too hot.

examples.ko: 헤어드라이어만 있으면 빨리 준비할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With just a hair dryer, I can get ready fast.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '드라이어'나 '드라이기'라고 많이 말해요. 머리를 말리는 일은 '드라이하다'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: In daily life people often shorten it to '드라이어' or '드라이기'. Drying hair is also sometimes called '드라이하다'.

examples.en: The taste stayed on the tip of my tongue for a long time.
I lightly licked the ice cream with the tip of my tongue.
That name is just on the tip of my tongue.
The words came right up to my tongue, but I held back.

examples.ko: 혀끝을 윗니 뒤에 대고 발음해 보세요.
examples.en: Try pronouncing it with the tip of your tongue behind the upper teeth.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 차를 마셨더니 혀끝은 아직도 얼얼해요.
examples.en: I drank hot tea, and the tip of my tongue is still numb.

explain: 혀의 맨 끝부분이에요. 맛이 남는다고 말할 때나 발음을 설명할 때 '혀끝에 남다', '혀끝을 대다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the very end of the tongue. It's often used in phrases like '혀끝에 남다' (linger on the tongue) when describing taste and '혀끝을 대다' (touch with the tongue tip) when explaining pronunciation.

examples.en: This shop only accepts cash.
I had no cash, so I paid by card.
If you pay in cash, I'll give you a small discount.

examples.ko: 현찰은 잃어버릴까 봐 조금만 가지고 다녀요.
examples.en: I only carry a little cash in case I lose it.
I went to the bank and withdrew cash.

examples.ko: 요즘은 현찰 없이도 지하철을 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: These days you can ride the subway without cash.

explain: '현금'과 같은 뜻이고, '현찰'은 말할 때 더 편하게 써요. 카드나 계좌이체의 반대로 눈앞에서 내는 돈을 말해요. '현찰로 내다', '현찰만 받다'처럼 가게에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '현금', but '현찰' sounds more casual in speech. It stands against cards or bank transfers and means money handed over on the spot. You often hear it in shops, as in '현찰로 내다' or '현찰만 받다'.

en: born in the year of the tiger

examples.en: I was born in the year of the tiger, so I like tiger pictures.
My father and I are both tigers by zodiac sign.
People often say those born in the year of the tiger are brave.
People of the same tiger sign differ in age by multiples of twelve.

examples.ko: 내 친구 중에 호랑이띠가 세 명이나 있어요.
examples.en: Three of my friends are tigers by zodiac sign.
Are you also a tiger by zodiac sign like me, teacher?

explain: '띠'는 태어난 해를 12가지 동물로 나타내는 거예요. 한국에서는 나이를 직접 묻기 어려울 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물어서 대략 나이를 알기도 해요. '호랑이띠' 외에 '소띠', '토끼띠'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '띠' assigns each birth year to one of 12 animals. In Korea, when it feels awkward to ask age directly, people ask '무슨 띠예요?' to get a rough idea. Other signs are said the same way, such as '소띠' and '토끼띠'.

examples.en: I ate pumpkin porridge when I had a cold.
Pumpkin porridge is sweet and smooth, so it's tasty.
I put glutinous rice balls into the pumpkin porridge.
Please pack just one bowl of pumpkin porridge.
The pumpkin porridge went cold, so I heated it up again.
I had a simple meal of pumpkin porridge.

explain: 호박을 삶아 곱게 으깨고 쌀가루 등을 넣어 끓인 단맛 나는 죽이에요. 죽을 만드는 걸 '죽을 쑤다'라고 해서 '호박죽을 쑤다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a sweet porridge made by boiling pumpkin, mashing it smooth and cooking it with rice flour and other ingredients. Making porridge is '죽을 쑤다', so you say '호박죽을 쑤다'.

examples.en: My grandmother gave me a ripe persimmon.
A ripe persimmon has thin skin and is very sweet.
The persimmon ripened and turned soft.

examples.ko: 가을에 홍시 한 상자를 선물 받았어요.
examples.en: In autumn I received a box of ripe persimmons as a gift.
I was so embarrassed that my face turned red like a ripe persimmon.
I tried making jam from ripe persimmons.

explain: 단단한 '단감'과 달리 푹 익어서 말랑해진 감이에요. 껍질을 말려서 먹는 '곶감'과도 달라요. 얼굴이 빨개진 걸 '홍시처럼'이라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: Unlike the firm '단감', this is a persimmon that has ripened until soft and squishy. It is also different from '곶감', which is dried. People sometimes describe a flushed face as being 'red like 홍시'.

examples.en: The mussel broth is really refreshing.
I added mussels and boiled a soup.
You have to wash mussel shells clean.

examples.ko: 홍합이 입을 벌리면 다 익은 거예요.
examples.en: When the mussels open their shells, they are done.
I added mussels and clams together.
I made the jjamppong broth with mussels.

explain: 검은색 긴 껍데기를 가진 조개류예요. 국물 맛이 시원해서 탕이나 짬뽕에 많이 넣어요. 보통 '조개'와는 모양이 달라서 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is a shellfish with a long dark shell. Its broth tastes clean and refreshing, so it is often added to soups and jjamppong. Its shape differs from typical '조개' (clams), so it has its own name.

examples.en: The fire alarm suddenly went off and startled me.
Every building must install a fire alarm.
Please check the fire alarm battery.
Fire alarms are usually attached to the ceiling.
A strange sound is coming from the fire alarm.
We started the evacuation drill with the fire alarm.

explain: 불이 났을 때 소리로 알려 주는 기계예요. '화재경보기가 울리다'처럼 '울리다'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 건물 안전 안내문에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a device that warns of fire with a sound. It usually pairs with '울리다', as in '화재경보기가 울리다'. You often see it in building safety notices.

examples.en: There is a farewell party for the department head tomorrow.
At the farewell party, my colleagues gave me gifts.

examples.ko: 유학 가는 친구를 위해 환송회를 열었어요.
examples.en: We held a going-away party for our friend who is going to study abroad.
We need to book a place for the farewell party.
I'm sorry I couldn't come to the farewell party.
Like welcome parties, farewell parties are held as a work dinner.

explain: 떠나는 사람을 위해 하는 모임이에요. 새로 온 사람을 맞이하는 '환영회'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요. 비슷한 말로 '송별회'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a gathering held for someone who is leaving. It is good to learn it as a pair with '환영회', which welcomes a newcomer. A similar word is '송별회'.

examples.ko: 오늘은 회색빛 하늘 때문에 기분이 가라앉아요.
examples.en: Today the gray sky is making me feel down.

examples.ko: 비가 오기 전에 하늘이 회색빛으로 변했어요.
examples.en: Before the rain, the sky turned gray.
I bought a coat with a grayish tone.
Her hair started to take on a gray tint.

examples.ko: 안개 낀 아침 거리는 온통 회색빛이었어요.
examples.en: The foggy morning street was gray all over.
Gray gives a calm feeling.

explain: '회색'이 색 이름이라면 '회색빛'은 그 색이 도는 빛깔이에요. '잿빛'도 비슷하게 쓰지만, 둘 다 우울하거나 흐린 분위기를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: If '회색' is the color name, '회색빛' is the grayish hue. '잿빛' is used in a similar way, and both often appear when describing a gloomy or overcast mood.
